built.what: The contract type: entityId declaration (builder + parser), provenance, freshness, and the document/version/placement shapes. Authored LOCALLY per OR-A1 with the operator-set promotion criterion (promotes when G-34 closes) recorded in the file header.
Drizzle schema for the three tables, with the four columns the brokerage table lacks, unique indexes carrying the store-once and idempotent-placement guarantees, and DB-level closed-set CHECKs.
Hand-authored idempotent migration matching the repo convention (no drizzle meta journal in this repo; existing migrations are hand-written SQL).

The store: createDocument (idempotent on entityId), placeDocument (one placement row, no document/version write), reviseDocument (supersede + insert + move pointer in ONE transaction with SELECT FOR UPDATE), readDocument (stamps every read), countDocumentRows (measured counts with their counting rules).
23 contract tests including the both-directions STALE proof and the entityId reconstruction-trap cases.

11 store probes against a real Postgres, written at the SCHEMA level deliberately: a store-layer test could satisfy the guarantees with application discipline and leave the table free to violate them.
Hand-added the three tables, three PKs, nine indexes, two FKs across the dump's three sections.
Added the three tables to the hardcoded expected-table list (a known CI hazard for any new ldt table).

findings.title: The engine document-ingest mechanism is reachable only over HTTP, not by import — OR-A2 is implementable but not as a package dependency
findings.evidence: @hauska-engine/document-ingest is `"private": true` (packages/document-ingest/package.json) and its blob index writes the `document_blobs` table in the ENGINE's database (packages/document-ingest/src/pg-blob-index.ts:2-3). legacy-design-tools has ZERO dependency on any hauska-engine package (grep of package.json and artifacts/api-server/package.json returns nothing). dataroomIngest.ts reaches it via postEngineSpine over process.env.ENGINE_API_URL.
findings.why_it_matters: OR-A2 said reuse the mechanism. That ruling is honored, but the seam is an HTTP call to engine-api, not an import — so Smart Files cannot call pinBlob directly and the CID is minted engine-side. The store records the CID and never re-implements content addressing, which is the substance of the ruling. Recording the shape so a later lane does not try to add a package dependency that does not exist.
findings.disposition: Implemented as documented in the store header. No operator action needed.

findings.title: The port interface cleanly separates blob-pinning from claim-atom writing, so Smart Files needs only half of it
findings.evidence: packages/document-ingest/src/port.ts declares DocumentBlobStore (pinBlob/fetchBlob, 'Idempotency is a port contract: pinBlob dedups on content hash') separately from DocumentAtomStore (writeDocumentAtom, dedups on atom DID), combined only in DocumentIngestStore.
findings.why_it_matters: Smart Files stores DOCUMENTS, not extracted claims. It needs the blob half and no claim extraction. Good news for OR-A2: reuse does not drag in the classification pipeline.

adversarialReview.conducted: planner, CP2, against the built artifact

challenges.challenge: Do the store probes actually test the SCHEMA, or would they pass on a schema that permits the violation?
challenges.resolution: They test the schema. The probes run raw SQL against the built tables rather than calling the store module, and four of them assert specific PG SQLSTATEs (23505 unique violation, 23514 check violation) for the second-document, duplicate-placement, version-reuse, bad-policy and bad-target cases. A store-module test would have proven only that MY code is disciplined, leaving the table free to be violated by the next writer.

challenges.challenge: Is store-once actually guaranteed, or merely conventional?
challenges.resolution: Guaranteed by a unique index on smart_file_documents.entity_id, and separately by a unique index on (document_id, target_type, target_id) for placements. Without the second one, 'placed in three locations' could legitimately read as four. Both are asserted by probe, not just declared.

No, structurally: placements reference the document and resolve version through document.current_version, so there is no per-placement write to partially fail. reviseDocument does the supersede + insert + pointer move in one transaction with SELECT FOR UPDATE on the document row, so two concurrent revisions cannot both compute the same nextVersion — and if one somehow did, the (document_id, version) unique index refuses it.

challenges.challenge: Does the freshness design permit content to be served without a stamp?
challenges.resolution: No read path returns content without freshness: readDocument builds the stamp unconditionally, and SMART_FILE_READ_SCHEMA requires it, with a probe asserting a stamp-less read is rejected. servedAt is taken as an ARGUMENT rather than read from a clock inside the evaluator, which is what makes the backdate test possible at all.

challenges.challenge: Is the hand-edited fixture a durability risk (DEV_PROCESS 6.3)?
challenges.resolution: Partly, and it is stated rather than hidden. It is a generated artifact I edited by hand because no live DB was available. I validated it structurally and reconciled it against the migration, but the authoritative regeneration (refresh-schema-fixture.sh against a DB with 0078 applied) is still owed. Flagged in the PR body and in notProven.

challenges.challenge: Does anything here let a caller believe a missing document is an honest absence?
challenges.resolution: readDocument returns null, and both the store header and the PR body state explicitly that this is NOT a typed absence and must not be rendered as a data gap until G-34. That is a documented constraint rather than an enforced one, which is weaker than a mechanism — recorded honestly as such rather than claimed as safe.
